subject: Physics
central_question: How do disturbances propagate as waves, and how are travelling waves, their speeds, superposition, reflection, standing modes and beats described quantitatively?
in_scope_units: 14.1 Introduction — waves as propagating disturbances carrying energy/information without bulk transport of matter; mechanical, electromagnetic and matter waves.
14.3 Displacement relation in a progressive wave, including amplitude, phase, wavelength, angular wave number, period and frequency.
14.4 Speed of a travelling wave — v = νλ, transverse waves on strings and longitudinal sound waves.
14.6 Reflection of waves, standing waves and normal modes in strings and air columns.
banned_topics: Detailed isolated simple harmonic motion from the previous chapter
Electromagnetic-wave theory beyond the chapter introduction

known_pitfalls.claim: A mechanical wave transports the medium bodily from source to receiver.
known_pitfalls.correction: The disturbance propagates while the medium’s particles oscillate about equilibrium; there is no bulk flow of matter with the wave.

known_pitfalls.claim: All waves require a material medium.
known_pitfalls.correction: Mechanical waves require a medium, but electromagnetic waves such as light can travel through vacuum.

known_pitfalls.claim: A travelling-wave speed is set by its frequency alone.
known_pitfalls.correction: For the non-dispersive mechanical waves treated here, the medium determines the speed; source frequency and v then fix λ through v = νλ.

known_pitfalls.claim: A pulse reflected from a rigid boundary keeps the same phase.
known_pitfalls.correction: Reflection from a rigid boundary produces a phase change of π; reflection from a free/open boundary has no phase reversal.

known_pitfalls.claim: A pipe closed at one end supports all harmonics.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter’s closed-open air column supports only odd harmonics.
